thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: Shoreline (enterprise, private VPC) - multiple customer-facing endpoints returning 502/504 from NLB targets — suspected ingress/egress path disruption. Severity: P1. Affected: dedicated tenant pool 42, some ALB-backed services. First seen: 2025-11-12T09:10:56Z
oncall-amber: taking the page. @eng-net-julio can you validate NLB target group health and SG rules? I'll start customer comms.
eng-net-julio: checking target group health now — 3/6 targets unhealthy, healthchecks timing out. NLB reports connection reset. pulling target logs.
sre-lead-hannah: tagging in. any recent infra changes? route53, SG, or NAT updates?
ops-eli: no deploys in last hour according to deploy-bot, but we did push a security group cleanup at 08:45 that affected ephemeral egress rules in the shared infra account. rolling that back now as a precaution.
deploy-bot: Recent activity: security-group-cleanup-job (08:45) — automated rule prune on tenant-hosting-subnet.
oncall-amber: @cs-jane I started a customer message: "We are investigating increased 5xx rates for requests to your private endpoints. No data access impact expected. We'll update in 15m."
shoreline-netops-bob: seeing SYNs arriving at NLB then immediate RST from targets. From inside their VPC, backends can reach the internet fine. Could be egress path from our NAT/egress proxies or SG blocking return traffic.
eng-net-julio: collection: `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:tg:42` shows ip-targets failing TLS handshake timeouts. grabbing tcpdump from one target: `tcpdump -nni eth0 port 443` — lots of SYN, no ACK from our proxy at 10.81.2.17.
sre-lead-hannah: possibility: conntrack exhaustion / asymmetric SNAT after SG prune. @ops-eli any signs of conntrack alerts?
ops-eli: conntrack meters spiked around 08:46 on natgw-02, concurrent with the SG prune job. we have partial mitigation plan: flip routes for tenant pool 42 to natgw-03 and add temporary direct-egress ACL to bypass pruned rules. preparing to apply.
oncall-amber: do the route flip but coordinate TTL changes for Route53 if we need traffic steering. want minimal DNS churn.
eng-net-julio: prepared commands to update route table association for subnet group 42: `aws ec2 replace-route-table-association --association-id rta-abc123 --route-table-id rtb-03` — will apply once SRE confirms.
sre-lead-hannah: go ahead with route flip to natgw-03 now. also increase conntrack table on natgw-03 if possible: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144` on the appliance. ops-eli can you exec?
ops-eli: doing sysctl now on natgw-03. applying route table replace in 2m and watching.
(ops-eli posted reaction :hourglass_flowing_sand:)
shoreline-netops-bob: after route flip we can run targeted health checks from Shoreline end to confirm backend completes handshake. will hold until you say done.
eng-net-julio: route flip executed at 09:15:40Z. targets recovering: now 5/6 healthy. connection resets dropping.
oncall-amber: updating customer: "We routed your VPC's egress through an alternate NAT and are seeing backend health recoveries. We're continuing monitoring and will confirm full recovery."
cs-jane: noted. customer asked for root cause and ETA for permanent fix.
sre-lead-hannah: immediate RCA draft: automated SG cleanup removed a needed ephemeral allow rule for our egress proxy -> tenant return path, causing asymmetric return and conntrack spike on natgw-02. Mitigation: route flip to natgw-03 and restored ephemeral allow on security-group-tenant-egress. Next steps: revert aggressive prune job, add canary run, and add post-prune validation that simulates tenant return flow.
oncall-amber: I'm handing over to @sre-lead-hannah for postmortem and follow-ups. @shoreline-netops-bob please confirm when you have full traffic patterns normal.
shoreline-netops-bob: traffic looks normal from our side, error rate back down to baseline over 10m. will send logs for your postmortem.
sre-lead-hannah: creating incident postmortem ticket and action items: 1) revert prune, 2) add validation harness, 3) increase conntrack alert sensitivity, 4) safe-mode for SG prunes. ETA for next update: 2025-11-12T11:00Z.
oncall-amber: closing the on-call handoff. I'll remain available if Shoreline asks. great team work, :thumbsup:.
incident-bot: Incident marked RESOLVED at 09:23:40Z (duration ~13m). Summary posted to #incidents-log and automated customer followup scheduled.
